name: US equity stress
summary: S&P 500 4.3% below its high and VIX 20.6 on 10 Nov, both easing but VIX still just inside the Watch band
state: The S&P 500 traded near 7,479 late on 10 Nov, 4.3% below its 52-week high of 7,819 and 2.7% lower on the week, after a worst single day of -4.4% in the past five sessions (Yahoo Finance). The VIX was 20.6, down from 25.6 at the 6 Nov close but still just above the 20 line that marks Watch. A hotter-than-expected October CPI report on 10 Nov weighed on stocks during the session.
for_you: Pensions, ISAs and other stock-market savings are exposed to swings while volatility stays elevated. Short-term falls of this size are common and have often reversed; the gauges are well short of crisis levels.
rubric_hit: VIX 19.5 has not yet cleared the 18 exit line, so Watch holds
why: The S&P 500 is the world's risk barometer; sharp falls and spiking volatility transmit to pensions, credit and confidence globally.
drivers: Earnings, interest-rate expectations, liquidity, geopolitical shocks, positioning and leverage.

rubric.alert: VIX > 30, or drawdown > 15%, or a market-wide circuit breaker trips.
rubric.normal: VIX < 20 and S&P 500 drawdown from 52-week high < 5%.
